verdicts.evidence: 450 runs on small synthetic problems (q∈{0.5,2,5}, a few ρ values) confirm convergence to 1e-16 residuals and blockwise optimality to 5e-10; mutation removing Assumption 2.6 causes infeasibility. But the setup is a clearly reduced synthetic instance, not a full-scale problem.

Toy problem with scaled nonlinearity (q=2, 48 initializations × 3 ρ per cell) shows linear contraction factors ~0.06 for small ‖C‖ and degradation to >0.998 at ‖C‖=25–50. Real numbers address the claim but on a small synthetic stand-in; exact threshold untestable since constants m1,m2,m3 are unspecified.

Toy problem with box constraints (4 cells, 12 seeds each) shows geometric gap decay (factor ≤0.0881) with all constraints active at the limit (no second-order differentiability), and 19,200 local-min probes find no better point. Mutation breaking eq. 4 destroys convergence. Setup is a small synthetic instance.

Sympy derivation independently confirms all quadratic coefficients carry Δt-exponent exactly 3 (p=3.0000 fit), and simulation on a small instance (T=6, N=2, m=2kg) shows linear contraction ~0.71 across Δt∈{0.002…0.1}; mutation rescaling by Δt⁻³ destroys convergence. The simulation is a reduced setup, not the full locomotion pipeline.

The q≥10 transition was tested (10 q-values × 6 hyperparameter settings × 6 seeds) but no sublinear regime was found below q=10 and no transition at q=10; the paper does not report μ_x, μ_z, ρ so the exact setup cannot be matched. The baseline comparison (PADMM, IPDS-ADMM, IADMM) was not attempted at all due to missing problem instances, dimensions, and hyperparameters.

No experiments were run: real robot experiments require unavailable hardware with no released code/models/logs, and the 2D simulation curves of Figure 5 cannot be matched because T, contact schedule, target CoM, initial state, and ρ are not reported. Only partial overlap with Claim 4's small simulation exists.

overall: The logbook provides toy-scale numerical evidence and mutation tests that support the paper's theoretical convergence claims (Theorems 3.1–3.3, Corollary 4.2) on small synthetic problems, including a symbolic verification of the O(Δt³) scaling. However, the empirical baseline comparisons and real-robot experiments are not reproduced due to missing problem specifications, unreleased code, and unavailable hardware.
